title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-v9
content:
Purpose / context:
- Back-of-envelope to validate price points for self-serve hosted API + simple tier ideas (incl. embeddings).
- Focus: unit economics per token, rough margins, plausible free/dev/growth tiers, and a sketch for reserved/dedicated pricing.
- Not final — rough assumptions here, need engineering perf numbers + infra cost breakdown to finalize.

Assumptions (baseline, changeable):
- Model mix: 60% small gen (chat-like, <256 tokens output), 30% mid (256-1024 tokens), 10% long (>1024).
- Avg tokens per request: prompt 60 tokens, response 180 tokens => 240 tokens total per call (for gen).
- Embeddings: average vector request = 512-dim, 0.5 tokens per token-equivalent? (we price per 1k embedding units).
- Serving infra cost: effective infra cost (GPU amortized + infra + SRE + network) = $0.0005 per 1k tokens (hosted) as current rough estimate.
  - This maps to $0.0000005 per token. (HIGHLY approximate; confirm with infra team)
- Variable overhead: storage, logs, tracing, caching = additional $0.0001 per 1k tokens.
- Cost of sales, support, experiments, R&D allocation to hosted = ~30% markup on infra variable cost when thinking of contribution margin.

Unit economics sample math (hosted API):
- Using infra cost 0.0005 / 1k tokens => 0.0000005 / token.
- Add infra overhead 0.0001 / 1k => 0.0000001 / token.
- Total variable cost per token = 0.0000006.
- Add GAAP-ish overhead (support+CS+marketing) ~ 30% => target gross margin built on price P: margin = (P - 0.0000006)/P.

Translate to per-1k-token price (market comps):
- Typical market: $0.003 / 1k tokens (low-end), $0.01 / 1k (mid), $0.03+ /1k (premium).
- If P= $0.003/1k => cost 0.0006/1k -> variable fraction = 0.2 -> huge margin. Wait — reconcile units: our cost above is 0.0006 per 1k (not 0.0000006). Recalculate carefully:
  - I intentionally left ambiguous earlier. Recompute: assume infra effective cost = $0.20 per GPU-hour; throughput ~200k tokens/s (model dependent)?? TOO MANY DEPENDS. Simpler approach below.

Simpler cost model (componentized):
- GPU cost amortized per token: take a small-ish model served on an A100-ish node: assume cost-per-token = $0.0005 / 1k tokens (conservative); (i.e., $0.0000005/token).
- Control plane, storage, networking etc = $0.0002 / 1k tokens.
- Total base cost = $0.0007 / 1k tokens.
- Add S&M + G&A + R&D allocation = $0.0013 / 1k tokens -> target price to hit 60% gross margin = ~$0.00325 / 1k tokens.

Rule-of-thumb: if base variable cost ~ $0.0007/1k -> we can set a low-entry price at $0.003/1k and still be profitable at scale for hosted. But verify with infra (this feels optimistic).

Per-request example: 240 tokens => 0.24 * (price per 1k tokens).
- At $0.003/1k => per request = $0.00072. So 1,000 requests = $0.72.

Tier sketches (hosted self-serve):
- Free: 50k tokens / month (good for quick eval, ~200 sample requests)
- Developer: $19/mo => credits = 2M tokens (=> effective price $0.0095/1k for small monthly commitment; this is okay because CLV of self-serve devs is small)  <-- need to decide if we want credit packs or pure usage billing.
- Starter: $99/mo => 12M tokens (~$0.00825/1k) aimed at single-product small apps.
- Growth: $499/mo => 75M tokens (~$0.00665/1k) for heavier usage and early scale.
- Scale/Business: $2,500/mo => 500M tokens (~$0.005/1k) with higher rate-limits and SLOs.
- Enterprise: custom, includes dedicated capacity pricing (see below), committed discounts.

Notes on that tiering:
- These are usage-credit based pricing (prepaid monthly buckets) rather than pure per-token metering to make costs predictable for customers.
- We can offer overage per 1k tokens at $0.003/1k (if embedded above tiers) or block charges.
- Need to simulate arithmetic vs. pure metered billing (some customers prefer pay-as-you-go with per-1k price instead of credits).

Embeddings pricing idea:
- Base: $0.01 per 1k embedding units (where 1 embedding unit ~ 1 512-dim vector request).
- Volume discount: 10% @ 10M units, 25% @ 100M units.
- Rationale: embedding compute is cheaper per vector than gen (no autoregressive decode), but storage and vector search infra (FAISS/HNSW) cost is material.

Dedicated / Reserved (Dedicated & Private):
- Committed monthly capacity (example): small pool (1x4-GPU) => $X/month (need cost calc). Quick back-of-envelope: 4xA100 cost (cloud) ~ $24/hr * 24 * 30 = $17k/mo raw infra -> add infra mgmt + margin => list $25k/mo? This is in line with enterprise reserved pricing for capacity.
- Offer simple pricing bands:
  - Dedicated-Small: $8k/mo (shared 16GB-class GPUs) - for low-throughput non-critical workloads
  - Dedicated-Medium: $25k/mo (4x A100-equivalent) - predictable throughput ~ Y tokens/sec
  - Dedicated-Large: $80k+/mo (multi-node clusters) - custom SLA.
- Also allow burst credits for hosted fallback (to avoid downtime during scaling spikes).

Key questions / TODOs:
- Get precise infra token-level cost from infra team: cost per 1k tokens for our most common served model families (small/mid/large).
- Confirm throughput numbers (tokens/sec) per instance for our common model variants (for accurate dedicated pricing).
- Decide billing model for self-serve: prepaid token packs vs pure metered monthly billing. Tradeoffs: predictability vs stickiness.
- Discounts & coupons: how deep for startups? sales motion needs thresholds.
- Embedding unit definition to standardize across dimensions. For example: define 1 embedding unit = 1 request of up to 1024 tokens or 1 vector up to 1536 dims? Need ops input.

Open thoughts:
- Consider offering a mid-tier pure pay-as-you-go price at $0.003/1k and an optional discounted subscription (e.g., $499/mo for 75M tokens) for committed customers.
- Introduce model/compute class labels (small/mid/large/custom) and surface in billing: e.g., small models at $0.003/1k, large (GPT-style) at $0.01/1k. That prevents self-serve sticker shock for customers using tiny models vs big models.
- For Dedicated, price by baseline qps and peak qps SLA instead of raw GPUs to make procurement simpler for customers.

Short checklist next steps:
- [ ] Infra: token-cost-by-model (small/mid/large) by 2026-03-10 (ask Ryan in infra).
- [ ] SRE/ops: throughput per instance and variance across sequence lengths.
- [ ] Legal: confirm wording for committed discounts and overage rules.
- [ ] Growth: run price-sensitivity quick survey in N=50 existing trial accounts.

Notes to self: rough, messy. Keep pushing numbers to be conservative for margins (i.e., assume higher infra cost). Reconcile units carefully (always specify $/1k tokens).
